# omarchy-zfs

> omarchy-zfs is a native Arch Linux package that adds root-on-ZFS and ZFSBootMenu
> support to Omarchy Linux (DHH's Arch + Hyprland distribution), version Quattro (4.x)
> and later. It is a support layer that depends on stock Omarchy — not a fork.

## What it does

- Makes `omarchy update` safe on a ZFS root. Stock Omarchy overwrites its mkinitcpio
  HOOKS drop-in on every update, which silently removes the `zfs` initramfs hook and
  leaves the system unbootable. omarchy-zfs installs a PostTransaction pacman hook
  that runs last in every transaction and re-asserts the zfs hook, then regenerates
  the initramfs and ZFSBootMenu.
- Takes an automatic ZFS snapshot before every pacman transaction (PreTransaction
  hook with retention), replacing snapper/Limine snapshots. Rollback is done by
  booting the snapshot from ZFSBootMenu.
- Removes stale btrfs-only snapper configs that otherwise make `omarchy update`
  abort permanently on ZFS roots.
- Keeps ZFSBootMenu first in the EFI BootOrder (Limine, a hard Omarchy dependency,
  can silently front-load itself — a dead boot on ZFS). It only reorders, never
  deletes other bootloaders' entries.
- Blocks kernel upgrades that the installed ZFS module (zfs-dkms or prebuilt)
  cannot support, preventing kernel/ZFS version skew.
- Monthly `zpool scrub` systemd timer, zvol-swap hibernation setup, native ZFS
  encryption unlock hook for ZFSBootMenu, manual snapshot create/restore tools,
  and `omarchy-bootstrap-zfs` for laying down pool + datasets + ZFSBootMenu on
  fresh installs or disaster recovery.

## Install

- Existing Omarchy system on a ZFS root: `yay -S omarchy-zfs` (AUR:
  https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/omarchy-zfs). Dependencies resolve via the
  virtual `zfs`/`zfs-utils` provides, so zfs-dkms, zfs-dkms-git, zfs-linux, or
  zfs-linux-lts all work. ZFSBootMenu itself is an optdepend (AUR package or
  prebuilt EFI images from zfsbootmenu.org).
- Fresh machine: the omarchy-zfs ISO (beta) — the official Omarchy installer plus a
  root-on-ZFS path, fully offline. Download:
  https://dl.omarchy-zfs.com/omarchy-zfs-2026.08.17-x86_64-quattro.iso
  or build it yourself from iso/ in the source repo (one command, needs docker).
- Caution: the AUR package named `omarchy` is an unrelated third-party placeholder.
  The real omarchy dependency is the official package from pkgs.omarchy.org, already
  present on every Omarchy system.

## Why ZFS instead of btrfs

Omarchy defaults to btrfs; omarchy-zfs exists because ZFS offers:
- Native whole-pool encryption as a dataset property (no LUKS layer); /etc, /var,
  logs, credentials, and machine-id are all covered, unlocked at boot by ZFSBootMenu.
- Raw encrypted replication: `zfs send --raw` ships snapshots to a TrueNAS box, S3,
  or any untrusted target without decrypting them — keys never leave the machine.
- One toolset from laptop to NAS: same snapshots, send/receive, and scrubs as
  ZFS-based NAS systems like TrueNAS.
- Bootable snapshots: ZFSBootMenu boots any snapshot or boot environment directly.
- Self-healing data: end-to-end block checksums, corruption repaired from redundancy,
  monthly zpool scrub timer included in the package.
- Multi-disk growth: mirrors and raidz1/2/3 supported by the installer, without
  btrfs's RAID5/6 write-hole caveats. zvols provide snapshot-able block devices
  (the package's hibernation swap is one); per-dataset compression/recordsize/quotas.

## Facts

- License: MIT. Author: Pete Jackson (peteonrails). Independent community project,
  not affiliated with Omarchy, 37signals, or OpenZFS.
- Default pool layout follows the archzfs / Arch-wiki convention.
- Package payload: /usr/bin/omarchy-zfs-* and omarchy-fs-* tools, libalpm hooks in
  /usr/share/libalpm/hooks, systemd scrub timer, /etc/zfsbootmenu reference config
  and hooks, /etc/omarchy-zfs/{autosnap.conf,bootorder.conf} (admin-editable).
